title: Senior's toolkit: renames, quick fixes and formatters
summary: The IDE refactorings, analyzers and formatter that keep code readable without arguing about it in review.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: renames, quick fixes and formatters
steps.body: Readable code is mostly kept readable by tools: a rename that cannot miss a caller, a quick fix that names a magic number, and a formatter and analyzers that CI enforces so reviews talk about design, not spacing.

toolkit.what: Rename a symbol everywhere it is used, including other files and projects. Unlike find-and-replace it only touches that symbol, never a lookalike in a string or another name.
flags: rename in Visual Studio (and in Rider's Visual Studio keymap)
toolkit.example: Put the cursor on calc, press F2, type CalculateLateFee, press Enter
toolkit.when: a name no longer says what the thing does

toolkit.what: Open quick actions and refactorings for the code under the cursor (Alt+Enter in Rider). The light bulb knows dozens of safe rewrites.
flags: turn a magic number like `0.2m` into a named `const`
flip a nested `if` into a guard clause
apply the same fix everywhere at once
toolkit.example: Cursor on 0.2m, Ctrl+., Introduce constant, name it VatRate

toolkit.what: Apply the formatting and code-style rules from `.editorconfig` to the whole solution. CI runs the check form so nobody formats by hand.
flags: change nothing; fail if anything would change (the CI form)
run only one part: spacing, code-style rules, or analyzer fixes
only fix diagnostics at this severity or higher

toolkit.what: The file at the repository root that sets the team's style and how loud each rule is. The IDE, `dotnet build` and `dotnet format` all read it.
flags: none, suggestion, warning or error for one rule
a section: the settings below apply to C# files

toolkit.what: Analyzer IDs you will see in warnings every week. Each one points at code that is dead or misleading. Look an ID up instead of silencing it.
flags: a private member is never used
a private member is assigned but its value is never read
the member uses no instance data, so it can be `static`

toolkit.what: Project settings that make the analyzers run on every `dotnet build`, not only in the IDE, so CI catches what the editor showed.
flags: IDExxxx style rules run during the build
which CAxxxx rule set is on, e.g. `latest-recommended`

steps.prompt: Match each analyzer ID to what it is telling you.
pairs: a private member is never used
a private field is written but never read
the method touches no instance data and could be static

steps.prompt: Your pull request fails in CI with this output. What do you do?
code: src/Billing/Invoice.cs(41,1): error WHITESPACE: Fix whitespace formatting. Replace 9 characters with '\n\s\s\s\s\s\s\s\s'. [src/Billing/Billing.csproj]
src/Billing/Invoice.cs(57,13): error IDE0011: Add braces to 'if' statement. [src/Billing/Billing.csproj]
options: Run `dotnet format` locally, check the diff, and commit the result
Fix the spacing by hand on line 41 and push again
Delete `.editorconfig` so the check has no rules
Add `--severity info` to the CI command so it stops failing
steps.explain: `--verify-no-changes` only reports. Plain `dotnet format` applies the same fixes, including the IDE0011 braces rule, so your local run makes CI pass. Never weaken the check to get green.

steps.prompt: A method called `Calc` is used in 14 files. There is also a class `CalcHelper` and a log message containing the word "Calc". What is the safe way to rename the method to `CalculateLateFee`?
options: Use the IDE's rename refactoring (F2 / Ctrl+R,Ctrl+R / Shift+F6) on the method
Find and replace `Calc` with `CalculateLateFee` in the whole solution
Rename it in its own file and fix the compile errors one by one
Add a new method and leave the old one for later
steps.explain: The rename refactoring follows the compiler's symbol, so it changes every call and nothing else. Find-and-replace would also break `CalcHelper` and the log text.

steps.prompt: The team decides an unused parameter should break the build. Complete the `.editorconfig` line.
steps.explain: IDE0060 is the unused-parameter rule and `error` fails the build. IDExxxx style rules only run in the build when the project sets `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`.

steps.prompt: Which tool do you reach for?
items: `0.2m` appears in the middle of a calculation
A nested `if` should become an early return
A teammate's branch has mixed tabs and spaces in 30 files
CI must reject code that does not follow the style rules

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Rename the moment a name stops fitting: with the refactoring it costs seconds. Run `dotnet format` before you push, and when a new warning ID shows up, read what it means before you suppress it, because most of them point at dead or misleading code.
